title: DeterministicResult
description: The normalised form of every application adapter result (master plan 4.5 check 2): status, identifiers, canonical values, errors, freshness and allowed next actions. No critical decision may depend on model prose, so an adapter result that does not normalise into this object is a schema_invalid error, never a partially trusted result. The adapter supplies every 'host' property; the core fills the 'alixai' ones (operation, capability_id) because it knows which call it made. Failures the core itself detects (adapter unreachable, timeout, malformed reply) are typed errors (common/error), not DeterministicResults: a DeterministicResult always records something the host reported.

operation.description: The adapter operation that produced this result. Set by the core from the call it made, never read from the adapter's reply.

capability_id.description: The capability the call was made for. Set by the core.

status.description: The outcome as the host reports it. ok: done as asked. rejected: the host refused (see errors). queued: accepted for asynchronous completion (see follow_up). partial: some of it happened (see errors). uncertain: the host cannot say whether it happened. unavailable: a host dependency is down. Only ok means success; every other value needs at least one error, except queued.

identifiers.description: Stable IDs of the records the result concerns (read, created, changed or cancelled).

values.description: Canonical values: the typed facts the host reports. Together with identifiers these are the only facts a verified response may state.

errors.description: Typed issues (ErrCode plus the field concerned). Empty exactly when status is ok or queued.

freshness.description: When and against which data version the result was produced. Required for ok, queued and partial; optional when the host could not read its data.

allowed_next_actions.description: The next steps the host will accept for this object. An empty list means none.

follow_up.description: Queued or deferred work the host reports. Required when status is queued.

preparation.description: What the host validated and would do, present exactly when operation is prepare and status is ok. The core builds the PreparedAction from it; the host proposes a risk level, the core decides the effective one.
The host's answer to Prepare: a canonical summary, the exact effects, the data versions the validation used, the risk level the host assigns and how long it will honour the preparation.

summary.description: Canonical one-sentence summary of the action.

effects.description: The exact effects and their targets. At least one: a preparation that changes nothing is a read.

data_versions.description: The versions of everything the validation relied on. At least one, so staleness is always detectable.

declared_risk_level.description: The risk level the host application assigns. The core may only raise it: the effective level is never below the platform minimum.

valid_for_seconds.description: How long the host will honour the preparation. The core never extends it.
